::: {.lead}
Today you start your course project: one topic, three files: a data sheet
(Excel), a report (Word) and a short talk (PowerPoint). There are no new
ideas: you use what you learned in Lectures 6–26. **Part A** is your own
project in the apps on the lab computer; **Part B** is on a simulator of
the interactive page: on paper, scan its QR code; on the screen, click its
link. After each step, write your result in its box.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a lab computer with Excel and Word, and an AI assistant
  that the university allows (for example `copilot.microsoft.com`). Save
  your files in your OneDrive: you go on with them in Lectures 29 and 30.
- **No lab computer today?** Do Part B of each experiment on your phone. Do
  Part A later on any computer with Office.
- **Choose one topic.** **Topic B · My study week:** your own study minutes
  for two weeks, every day (at least 14 rows: Day, Subject, Minutes). Only
  your own data. **Topic A · Canteen sales:** the canteen of Sunrise
  Company sold these items in four weeks (the list is also on the
  interactive page, to copy):

  | Week | Item     | Qty | Price (JD) |
  |:----:|----------|----:|-----------:|
  | 1    | Tea      | 40  | 0.5        |
  | 1    | Coffee   | 30  | 1          |
  | 1    | Water    | 20  | 0.25       |
  | 1    | Sandwich | 24  | 1.5        |
  | 1    | Cake     | 10  | 1          |
  | 2    | Tea      | 36  | 0.5        |
  | 2    | Coffee   | 34  | 1          |
  | 2    | Water    | 28  | 0.25       |
  | 2    | Sandwich | 20  | 1.5        |
  | 2    | Cake     | 12  | 1          |
  | 3    | Tea      | 44  | 0.5        |
  | 3    | Coffee   | 28  | 1          |
  | 3    | Water    | 32  | 0.25       |
  | 3    | Sandwich | 26  | 1.5        |
  | 3    | Cake     | 8   | 1          |
  | 4    | Tea      | 30  | 0.5        |
  | 4    | Coffee   | 36  | 1          |

- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive page, every step has a check that answers at
  once.

## Experiment 1 · A question and a plan

**The idea (Lectures 21, 25 and 26):** a project starts with **one clear
question** that your data can answer. Then plan the five parts: the
question, the data, the chart, the report headings and the slides. No
personal data of other people: no names, phone numbers or marks.

**Aim:** write the plan of your project in five lines.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Word)**
:::

1. Make a new Word document and save it as `plan.docx`. Write your plan in
   five lines: the question, the data, the chart, the report headings and
   the five slides.

   {{< record "My question … ; my data … ; my chart …" lines=3 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good plan, for example for Canteen sales: *What sells most in the
   canteen, by money and by count?*; 20 rows: week, item, quantity, price,
   with Total = Qty × Price; a column chart of the total by item; the
   headings Introduction, The data, Results, What I learned, AI use; five
   slides: title, question, chart, two insights, thanks.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which question can your study data answer?

   - [x] On which day of the week do I study the most minutes?

     Why: It is clear, and your own minutes can answer it.

   - [ ] Am I a good student?

     Why: Too vague: minutes cannot answer it.

   - [ ] What are my classmates' marks?

     Why: Other people's personal data: not allowed.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-14/sims/plan-checker.html" poster="../../week-14/sims/plan-checker.png" title="Plan Checker: your course project" >}}

2. In **Plan Checker**, do Task 2: make a plan for *My study week* that
   passes all five checks. Which answers were wrong because of personal
   data?

   {{< record "Wrong because of personal data: …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **"What are my classmates' marks?"** and **"screenshots of classmates'
   chats"**: other people's personal data is not allowed. Your own minutes
   are fine.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which data must you never collect for your project?

   - [x] the names and phone numbers of buyers

     Why: Personal data of other people stays out of your project.

   - [ ] the price of each item

     Why: A price is not personal data.

   - [ ] your own study minutes

     Why: Your own data is fine for your project.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · The data sheet

**The idea (Lectures 11, 25 and 26):** type the data into Excel, one row
for each record, and make it a **table** (**Ctrl + T**) with a total row.
Add a column with a **formula**, for example Total = Qty × Price.
Summarize it with a **PivotTable**, and make **one chart** with a title
that answers your question.

**Aim:** build the data sheet of your project.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Excel)**
:::

1. Type your data, starting in cell **A1**, and make it a table with a
   total row. Topic A: add the column *Total* with `=C2*D2`. Save the file
   as `project.xlsx`.

   {{< record "Rows … ; the total row shows …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   One row for each record: 20 rows for Topic A, at least 14 for Topic B.
   In a table, the formula of *Total* fills the whole column by itself.
   Check one row by hand, for example 24 cups at 0.5 JD = 12 JD.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="12" unit="JD" hint="Qty × Price: 24 × 0.5."}
   A row has Qty **24** and Price **0.5** JD. What does `=C2*D2` show?

   Why: 24 × 0.5 = 12 JD. Check one row by hand: then you trust the column.
   :::

2. Insert a PivotTable that answers your question (Topic A: Rows *Item*,
   Values *Total*; Topic B: Rows *Subject*, Values *Minutes*). Then make
   one chart of it, with a title that answers your question.

   {{< record "The Grand Total … ; my chart and its title …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   One row for each item or subject, and a **Grand Total that equals the
   total row** of the table. A column chart compares the items or the
   subjects; its title says what it shows, for example "Minutes of study
   by subject (two weeks)".
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   The Grand Total of your PivotTable is 340, but the total row of the
   table shows 360. What is wrong?

   - [x] The PivotTable misses some rows: Refresh it, or check its range.

     Why: Both totals come from the same data, so they must be equal.

   - [ ] Excel adds up wrong.

     Why: Excel adds right; the PivotTable does not have all the rows.

   - [ ] Nothing: the numbers are close.

     Why: Close is not equal: some data is missing.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-13/sims/pivot-lab.html" poster="../../week-13/sims/pivot-lab.png" title="Pivot Lab: summarize Rana's month" >}}

3. In **Pivot Lab**, make the summary that answers the question *Which week
   brought the most money?* Which Rows and Values do you choose, and which
   week is it?

   {{< record "Rows … ; Values … ; the week …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Rows Week, Values Sum of Total**: the third week, **112 JD**. The
   question decides the row field and the calculation.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Your question is "Which item sells most often?". Which Values do you
   choose?

   - [x] Count of sales

     Why: Count gives how often each item was sold.

   - [ ] Sum of Total

     Why: Sum gives the money, not how often.

   - [ ] Average of Total

     Why: Average gives the usual size of a sale.
   :::

## Experiment 3 · The first draft

**The idea (Lectures 6, 7, 9 and 25):** in Word, write the **headings**
first, with **Heading 1**: Introduction, The data, Results, What I
learned, AI use. Copy your chart in Excel and paste it into Word. An AI
tool can draft sentences: check every number in your data sheet, and
write the text in your own words.

**Aim:** write the first draft of your report.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the apps (Word and an AI assistant)**
:::

1. Make `report.docx` with the five headings, each with the style
   **Heading 1**: *Introduction*, *The data*, *Results*, *What I learned*,
   *AI use*. Copy your chart in Excel and paste it under *Results*.

   {{< record "My five headings … ; the chart is under …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   Five Heading 1 lines in this order, and the chart under *Results*. The
   Navigation Pane (**View › Navigation Pane**) shows the five headings.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   How does each part of the report start?

   - [x] with a Heading 1

     Why: A heading style makes the parts, the Navigation Pane and later the table of contents.

   - [ ] with a bold line in the Normal style

     Why: Bold text looks like a heading, but Word does not see a heading.

   - [ ] with an empty line

     Why: An empty line gives no title to the part.
   :::

2. Ask the AI assistant for two sentences about your summary: paste only
   the numbers of your PivotTable. Check each number in your data sheet,
   write the true sentences in your own words under *Results*, and add a
   first line under *AI use*.

   {{< record "What I checked … ; was anything wrong? …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   Every number of an AI sentence must be in your PivotTable. A good first
   AI-use line: "Two sentences of the Results were drafted with an AI
   tool; I checked every number with my PivotTable and wrote them in my
   own words."
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   An AI sentence has a number that is not in your PivotTable. What do you
   do?

   - [x] Correct it, or delete the sentence.

     Why: Every number of the report comes from your data.

   - [ ] Keep it: the AI knows more data.

     Why: The AI did not see more data; it invented the number.

   - [ ] Round it a little.

     Why: A wrong number stays wrong when you round it.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-05/sims/word-ai-lab.html" poster="../../week-05/sims/word-ai-lab.png" title="Word AI Lab: draft, sum up, rewrite, translate" >}}

3. In **Word AI Lab**, choose **Rewrite**. Compare the AI text with the
   memo and tap the wrong part.

   {{< record "The wrong part, and why" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **"You can also pick it up on Friday morning"**: the memo says nothing
   about Friday. A rewrite must not add new facts.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   What must an AI rewrite of your text never do?

   - [x] add new facts

     Why: A rewrite changes the words, not the facts.

   - [ ] change the tone

     Why: A new tone is the job of a rewrite.

   - [ ] make the text shorter

     Why: A shorter text is fine when every fact stays.
   :::
